notes.summary: Sampling theory is about choosing a part of the population and measuring how reliable the sample results are. JSO asks on sampling methods (random and non-random), allocation in stratified sampling, and standard errors.

concepts.title: Sampling methods
concepts.body:
• Random (probability): simple random (lottery, random numbers), stratified, systematic, cluster, multistage.
  • Non-random: judgment (purposive), quota, convenience.
  • Systematic: pick every k-th unit after a random start, k = N/n.
  • Stratified: split into homogeneous strata, sample from each. Proportional allocation: ni = n × Ni/N.
  • Cluster: randomly select whole groups (clusters).

concepts.title: Errors and standard error
concepts.body:
• Sampling error: arises because only a sample is studied; falls as n grows. Non-sampling error: mistakes in measurement, response, processing; present even in a census.
  • SE of mean = σ/√n. With finite population (SRSWOR) multiply by √((N − n)/(N − 1)).
  • SE of proportion = √(pq/n).
  • Number of SRSWOR samples of size n from N = NCn; with replacement = Nn.

varieties.name: Identify the sampling method
varieties.how: Ask: does every unit have a known chance (random) or is choice by judgment / quota (non-random)?

example.q: An interviewer is told to interview 30 men and 20 women, chosen as he likes. Which method?
steps: Fixed numbers from each group, but free choice inside the group.

varieties.name: Systematic interval and stratified allocation
varieties.how: k = N/n; proportional n_i = n × N_i/N.

example.q: Strata of size 300 and 700; total sample 40 (proportional). Find each sample size.

varieties.name: Standard error
varieties.how: SE(x̄) = σ/√n, SE(p) = √(pq/n); SE varies as 1/√n.

example.q: σ = 20, n = 25. Find SE of the mean.

tips: To halve the SE, make the sample 4 times larger.
Stratified sampling works best when strata are internally similar (homogeneous) but differ from each other.
Cluster sampling works best when each cluster is internally varied (heterogeneous).
traps: Judgment and quota sampling are NOT random sampling methods.
Non-sampling errors do not go away in a census; they may even increase.
SE of proportion uses pq/n inside the square root, not p/n.

questions.q: Which of the following is a NON-random sampling method?
questions.solution: In quota sampling the interviewer chooses units by his own judgment within fixed quotas, so units do not have a known chance of selection. The others are probability methods.

questions.q: A systematic sample of 60 units is to be drawn from a list of 1,200 units. The sampling interval k is:
questions.solution: k = N/n = 1200/60 = 20. After a random start between 1 and 20, every 20th unit is taken.

questions.q: A population has SD 12. The standard error of the mean for a random sample of size 36 is:
A population has two strata of sizes 600 and 400. A sample of 50 is taken with proportional allocation. The sample sizes from the two strata are:
In a sample of 96 people, 40% are found to be smokers. The standard error of the sample proportion is:
A sample of size 100 gives a certain standard error of the mean. To reduce this standard error to half, the sample size must be:
questions.solution:
SE ∝ 1/√n. Halving SE needs √n to double, i.e. n to become 4 times.
New n = 4 × 100 = 400.
